newsitem.title: USA: US Treasuries down sharply. [CORRECTED 18:52 GMT]
newsitem.headline: US Treasuries down sharply. [CORRECTED 18:52 GMT]

text.p: U.S. Treasuries were sharply lower in early afternoon trade on Thursday after real money accounts followed technically-driven speculative accounts onto the selling path, traders and analysts said.
"It was broad-based selling that came from a number of sources," said Patrick Dimick, trader and Treasury strategist at UBS Securities LLC.
After the Federal Reserve was again absent from the market as a buyer of coupons, the market traded through the 114-23, 114-24 (corrects from 115-23, 115-24) area on the March T-bond contract.

"That area was a huge support level and all of the day traders in the futures pit had that as their stop out," said Dimick. "Every day trader who was long liquidated their positions and that pushed (the March bond contract) down to about 114-18 (corrects from 115-18).
"At that point, we saw real money accounts coming in to sell cash 10-year notes, again liquidating long positions," said Dimick.
"Some Japanese and Middle Eastern accounts took profits in U.S. Treasuries," said Greg Carr, bond market analyst at A.G. Edwards & Sons.
